h1:
Sakon Nakhon Cafes
In Town & by Nong Han — Good Coffee, Chill Vibes, Great Photos
intro: Sakon Nakhon is a town where you can cafe-hop all day. A lot of people don't realize it has serious specialty coffee shops that roast their own beans, mixed in with cozy wooden-house cafes and lakeside spots where you can sip a coffee looking out over Nong Han at sunset. We've picked 12 places locals actually go to and reviews keep mentioning, with a clear split between the ones you can walk to in town and the ones worth driving out for the view — plus their standout drinks, location, opening hours and rough prices. We'll tell you straight which ones are good for working and which are mainly for photos.

blocks.html: Sakon Nakhon's cafes roughly split into three groups. The first is the specialty crowd who take beans and roasting seriously — good for black-coffee drinkers or anyone who wants to chat with the barista about bean profiles. The second is the homey, cozy garden cafes, good for settling in to work or bringing the family. The third is the spots by Nong Han or near landmarks, where you come mainly for the view and photo angles. We've ranked this list by which places get talked about most and where locals take visitors — it doesn't mean the ones lower down aren't good; each stands out in its own way. Read the highlights and the area first, then pick to suit the day.

A note on prices. The figures below are rough per-person estimates for one drink plus a dessert or one bakery item. Regular coffee in Sakon Nakhon runs about 55–80 THB a cup, while specialty shops or special menus like single-origin pour-overs go higher. Many cafes have a weekly closing day and some shut early in the afternoon, so check opening hours and the day off for each place before you set out — especially the ones you have to drive out of town for.

blocks.text: 12 Sakon Nakhon cafes the locals go to

items.name: Sniff Roastery / Sniff Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: The specialty coffee shop Sakon Nakhon coffee fans rate near the top. They roast their own beans seriously, with options from light fruity roasts to dark nutty ones, served from an espresso bar or a slow pour-over bar where you can chat with the barista. The roastery branch on the bypass has a dark-toned fit-out with a grass lawn for chilling and photo corners, while the other branch sits in the That Choeng Chum area near the clock tower, which is easier to reach in town. Good for black-coffee drinkers who want a serious cup.
items.meta: Bypass / That Choeng Chum · Mon–Fri 07:30–19:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–19:00

items.name: Guzzjung Cafe' & Alexkoff Roaster (Wat Phra That Choeng Chum junction)
items.blurb: A two-storey cafe right at the Wat Phra That Choeng Chum junction. The draw is sitting upstairs with the stupa as your backdrop — good photos all day. The coffee is self-roasted with several bean profiles to choose from, and the bakery and croissants are made fresh. There's another branch on the Mueang Mai side that leans co-working, with plugs and wifi. The location lets you walk straight over to pay respects at the temple afterward, so you can combine a cafe with the landmark in one trip.
items.meta: Wat Phra That Choeng Chum junction · Mon–Fri 08:00–19:00, Sat–Sun 09:00–19:00

items.name: Suk Kasem Coffee & Restaurant
items.blurb: A riverside cafe in the Sri Wicha area that Sakon Nakhon locals love for easygoing evenings — you get both coffee and food. There's a wide garden zone with a river view, and a warm, laid-back vibe that suits families who want to sip coffee and also order a proper rice-and-curry meal. It stays open late, so you can come catch the breeze at sunset. A good pick when you want a cafe where you can actually eat a full meal, not just dessert.
items.meta: Sri Wicha area, riverside · open late into the evening · closed Tuesdays

items.name: Raintree Cafe
items.blurb: A garden-vibe cafe where you sit under big trees. By day it's a cafe for coffee and homemade bakery; come evening it switches into a cocktail bar and you can stay late. There are both indoor and outdoor zones, and dogs are welcome. Good for a group of friends who want to keep chilling from afternoon into the night, moving from coffee to cold drinks all in one place.

items.name: Get Idea Coffee
items.blurb: An easy-to-reach roadside cafe in town with convenient parking out front. The draw is the arty atmosphere, with a corner displaying paintings — fun for photos. In the morning before 10am there are breakfast sets to order alongside your coffee, plus a full range of cake and dessert. Good for a quick breakfast or a short work session in town — this is the name people usually get when they ask for a cafe in the town centre.

items.name: Moka Fox
items.blurb: A Scandinavian-toned wooden-house cafe in a residential area, with both a cool indoor air-con zone and an outdoor zone under big trees. The standouts are matcha, Japanese milk tea and pour-over coffee. There's a kids' play corner, so it suits families, and the shady, leafy setting photographs well. Open from morning until 4pm, so it's good for a morning-to-midday visit when you want a quiet, uncrowded cafe.

items.name: Z Md Cafe' Specialty Coffee
items.blurb: A dark, modern-toned cafe in the centre of town with cool air-con, focused mainly on specialty coffee. It has both a speed bar and a slow bar, and the baristas can talk coffee in detail. There are mocktails too for the non-coffee crowd, and dogs are welcome. The in-town location is comfortable for working — good for anyone who wants serious coffee in a cool air-conditioned room without driving out of town.

items.name: Alice Cafe Sakon
items.blurb: An in-town cafe in white-and-wood tones — warm, clean-looking and good for photos. The menu items people praise are the coconut latte and the five-blend Thai tea, and there's homemade bakery. Prices are friendly, mostly under 100 THB a cup. Open daily, both weekdays and weekends, so it's good for an easy stop when you want coffee and cake on a relaxed budget in town.

items.name: Wehug Cafe
items.blurb: A minimal black-and-white cafe next to the new bus terminal — spacious and clean, with several zones to choose from. The menu covers it all: coffee, tea, milk drinks, dessert and light food, with a strawberry cake people order often. Prices are friendly, and the location is handy for anyone who's just gotten off a coach or is waiting for one — an easy place to rest and sip a coffee before moving on.
items.meta: Next to the new bus terminal · open 08:00–19:00

items.name: Sunday Morning Home & Cafe
items.blurb: A house cafe tucked down a soi, decorated in a homey minimal Korean style, with a little garden — warm enough that it feels like sipping coffee at home. It's strong on matcha, cocoa and homemade cake. Open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays. Good for anyone after a quiet corner and pretty, unhurried photos — just right for a pair or a small group.
items.meta: Soi in town · Mon–Fri 10:00–16:00, Sat–Sun 09:30–19:00 · closed Mondays

items.name: Unefille Cafe and Space
items.blurb: A white, European-style building on the road toward Pha Daeng, with green meadows around it. The bright, airy setting gives you plenty of photo angles. Standout menu items include strawberry cheesecake and a tamarind-honey-lime drink. Open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays. You do have to drive out of town a bit, but you get that wide-open, easy-on-the-eyes feel — good for photos and chilling over the meadow view.
items.meta: Toward Pha Daeng · Tue–Fri 09:00–17:30, Sat–Sun 09:00–18:00 · closed Mondays

items.name: Sonata's Cafe (Siberian husky cafe)
items.blurb: An out-of-town dog-themed cafe with a Siberian husky pen you can play in by timed rounds. The atmosphere is cute and warm, good for families and animal lovers. There's a full range of coffee, drinks and snacks, including matcha, coconut tart, pasta and light steaks. Open from late morning into the evening, closed Mondays. Good for playing with the dogs then settling in for a long coffee — it's not a serious-coffee spot, but it's a fun one.
items.meta: Out of town · open 10:00–19:00 · closed Mondays

blocks.title: Tips for getting the most out of Sakon Nakhon's cafes
blocks.html: If you want serious coffee, head straight to the specialty crowd like Sniff or Z Md, order a single-origin pour-over and chat with the barista about the beans. If you're there for photos and views, Guzzjung at the Wat Phra That junction lets you sit upstairs with a clear look at the stupa, while for the lakeside, go to Suk Kasem or sit at the Khu Sut viewpoint along Nong Han in the evening to catch the sunset. Out-of-town cafes like Moka Fox, Unefille and Sonata's mostly close Mondays and shut early in the afternoon, so check days and hours before you drive out — and bring some cash, since some places only take cards/QR while others still mainly take cash.

blocks.text: Pick a cafe by your style

items.name: Serious coffee, after a good cup
items.blurb: Sniff Roastery and Z Md Cafe' are the two specialty spots that roast their own and take beans seriously. Order a pour-over or off the espresso bar and chat with the barista — good for black-coffee drinkers.

items.name: For photos and the Nong Han view
items.blurb: Riverside Suk Kasem and Guzzjung at the Wat Phra That junction, where you can see the stupa from upstairs, both photograph well — then move on to the Khu Sut viewpoint along Nong Han in the evening.

items.name: Settle in, work, bring the family
items.blurb: Moka Fox and Sonata's have kids' play corners and dogs, while Guzzjung Mueang Mai and Raintree are comfortable for working or chilling from afternoon into the evening.

blocks.text: Sitting at a Nong Han cafe in the evening

blocks.html: Sakon Nakhon's charm is Nong Han, a large freshwater lake in the middle of town. In the evening the lakeside has a cool breeze and a lovely sunset, and a lot of people grab coffee or a drink from a cafe in town to bring down to the water. The Khu Sut viewpoint is a lakeside plaza that's been newly done up for relaxing and taking photos, while cafes with a direct water view like Suk Kasem are good for settling in over dinner. We'd suggest coming from about 4pm onward for the nice light and to avoid the heat.

items: Go in the evening — the Nong Han lakeside is at its prettiest and coolest from about 4pm to sunset; midday sun is too harsh to enjoy.
Check the cafe's day off first — many close Monday or Tuesday, and some shut at 4pm; out-of-town spots especially need checking.
Bring cash — most places take card/QR payment, but some small shops still mainly take cash, so keep some on hand.
Specialty can cost more — single-origin pour-overs or special beans run pricier than regular coffee, so check the menu before ordering.
Combine with a landmark — Guzzjung sits right at the Wat Phra That Choeng Chum junction, so after your coffee you can walk straight over to pay respects at the stupa.

blocks.text: Plan a Sakon Nakhon cafe-hopping day

blocks.html: If you have a day in Sakon Nakhon and want to make the rounds of the cafes, here's the order we'd run it in to line up with each place's opening hours. Start with serious coffee in the morning, move on to photo-friendly cafes midday, and finish by Nong Han in the evening. Swap the spots around to suit each one's day off.

items.activity: Open the day at Sniff Roastery
items.note: The self-roasting shop opens earliest — order a single-origin pour-over and chat beans with the barista, sitting on the grass lawn in the morning air.

items.activity: Move on to Guzzjung at the Wat Phra That junction
items.note: Sit upstairs for a view of the Phra That Choeng Chum stupa — great photos and a second coffee with a croissant.

items.activity: Walk over to pay respects at Phra That Choeng Chum
items.note: It's right next to the cafe, so you can walk straight there — a cafe and a landmark in one morning.

items.activity: Lunch at Suk Kasem Coffee & Restaurant
items.note: Riverside in the Sri Wicha area — order rice and curry to fill up, then move on to coffee. Main meal and dessert in one place.

items.activity: Work or chill at Z Md Cafe'
items.note: Town centre, cool air-con, serious specialty, with plugs and wifi — good for ducking out of the afternoon sun.

items.activity: Get photos at Alice Cafe or Sunday Morning
items.note: Clean white tones that photograph well — a light coffee before the light starts to soften.

items.activity: Take an iced coffee to the Khu Sut viewpoint by Nong Han
items.note: Sit and catch the breeze waiting for sunset — the light's best now, and lakeside photos are a treat.

items.activity: Dinner at a freshwater-fish restaurant by Nong Han
items.note: Fresh fish with the lake view — an easy way to close the day before heading back to your stay.

faq.q: Which Sakon Nakhon cafe has genuinely good coffee?
faq.a: For serious coffee drinkers, locals recommend Sniff Roastery and Z Md Cafe' Specialty Coffee. Both are specialty shops that roast their own beans and offer several profiles, from light fruity roasts to dark ones — order off the slow pour-over bar and chat with the barista. Guzzjung at the Wat Phra That junction also roasts its own, plus you get the stupa view.

faq.q: Which Nong Han lakeside cafes in Sakon Nakhon are good for chilling?
faq.a: Suk Kasem Coffee & Restaurant in the Sri Wicha area is a riverside cafe with a view where you can also order food, good for an easygoing evening. If you want to sit right by Nong Han, the Khu Sut viewpoint is a lakeside plaza where you can bring a coffee, catch the breeze and shoot the sunset. We'd suggest coming from about 4pm onward.

faq.q: Which cafes in central Sakon Nakhon are easy to walk to?
faq.a: In town there's Get Idea Coffee, roadside with easy parking and an art corner; Z Md Cafe', dark-toned, cool air-con and coffee-focused; Alice Cafe, white-and-wood tones and easy on the wallet; and Wehug Cafe next to the new bus terminal, good for a stop before catching a coach. All are in the town centre, no driving out far required.

faq.q: About how much does a Sakon Nakhon cafe cost per person?
faq.a: Regular coffee runs about 55–80 THB a cup, and one drink plus one dessert comes to around 70–180 THB per person. Specialty shops or special pour-over menus go higher, while riverside spots where you also order food, like Suk Kasem, run about 100–250 THB per person. Many places take card/QR, but it's worth carrying cash just in case.

faq.q: Which Sakon Nakhon cafes are okay to bring kids or dogs to?
faq.a: Moka Fox has a kids' play corner and a garden zone, good for families. Sonata's Cafe is a Siberian husky-themed cafe with a pen you can play in by timed rounds. Raintree Cafe and Z Md are dog-friendly. Check the day off first, since many close on Mondays.
